scope: Static source review of the ROOT score-result acceptance caller V1 and its compatibility with the reviewed stdlib helper API. No import, execution, test, B/SSH/systemd action, capture/result/receipt payload access, or score evaluation was performed.

reviewed_helper_contract.api: build_root_acceptance(*, result_raw, capture_raw, score_admission_raw, score_launch_raw, export_acceptance_raw, export_exact_stop_raw, export_binding_raw, export_manifest_raw, result_path=RESULT_PATH)
reviewed_helper_contract.compatibility: The caller supplies all eight required byte arguments by matching keyword names; the default fixed result path is consistent with the helper; the writer call passes an absolute SCORE_ACCEPTANCE.json path and uses the returned exact receipt bytes for its binding.

findings.finding: The review path is not fixed to the independently reviewed SOURCE_REVIEW_V1.json. Path.relative_to is lexical and the caller does not reject .. components, so a path syntactically under PREP can escape. Review validation accepts any status beginning PASS_SOURCE_ONLY and only searches the raw text for the helper SHA; it does not validate the expected review schema/candidate path/byte count/SHA fields. Thus an unrelated or fabricated file can satisfy the gate.
findings.required_fix: Require the exact review path and exact schema/status and candidate pin fields, then check the review file SHA against the supplied/bound digest.

findings.finding: The caller only checks that REMOTE.py matches the transport body byte count/SHA. It never reads AST_BINDING.json or proves that the transmitted reader is the reviewed capture V4 template with only the five actual admission/launch/invocation literals substituted. A self-consistent transport can therefore bind an unreviewed reader body while the helper accepts its stdout.
findings.required_fix: Bind the exact capture V4 template and its exact independent review; validate the actual AST_BINDING receipt, literal values from the exact score ADMISSION/LAUNCH, and AST equality after normalizing only those five literals. Include strict raw stdout/stderr/body joins and fixed transport schema/type checks.

findings.location: main(): helper import origin/post-import pin check
findings.finding: The pre-import helper bytes are pinned, but after import the code performs two separate read(HELPER) calls to form the post-import length/SHA pair. It does not ensure those two bytes came from one stable read or that the loaded code object came from the same stable file version. A concurrent replacement can make the origin claim ambiguous.
findings.required_fix: Use one stable bounded post-import read and compare its full pin to the pre-import bytes; if retaining dynamic execution, bind a stable file identity across the import and post-import check.
